newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ITALIAN RELEGATION BATTLE HOTS UP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ITALIAN RELEGATION BATTLE HOTS UP.

text.p: The battle to avoid relegation from serie A intensified on Sunday with Cagliari, Perugia and Piacenza all struggling manfully to escape the drop zone.

As Juventus moved closer towards their 24th league title with a 3-0 win over Roma on Saturday, Cagliari, who have flirted with danger almost every season since returning to the top flight in 1990, hinted at another Houdini act by recovering to beat Italian Cup finalists Vicenza 2-1.
Uruguayan defender Gustavo Mendez put the visitors in front with a first minute free-kick but Carlo Mazzone's side equalised with a scorching 25-metre free-kick from Roberto Muzzi in the 36th minute.
It was the 900th serie A match in Vicenza's history and their sixth consecutive away defeat in a season that has tailed off dramatically since they were leaders in November.

After the break, Sandro Tovalieri's 49th minute goal, and the 64th minute dismissal of Mendez for a second bookable offence, gave Cagliari three points which puts them ahead of Perugia on goal difference, but keeps them fourth from bottom.
To avoid the drop, Cagliari must catch Piacenza - three points ahead of them.
Piacenza, the only club in multi-national Serie A to spurn foreigners, earned a 0-0 draw at second from bottom Verona -- a result that virtually condemns the latter to the drop.

Third from bottom Perugia, managed by ex-Parma coach Nevio Scala, were encouraged at Udinese by a third minute goal from Marco Negri, only for Brazilian Marcio Amoroso to level the scores with a 21st minute goal which looked off-side.
The second-half turned on the 75th minute dismissal of Perugia's Marco Materazzi, one of five former Parma players in Scala's squad.
Within a minute, Dane Thomas Helveg scored the winner which left Perugia trailing Cagliari on goal difference. That should be resolved next week when the two clubs play each other.
Bottom-of-the-table Reggiana left four foreign players on the bench at Sampdoria -- and lost 3-0 to a team who had not won in its last four matches.
In stark contrast to the fate awaiting Reggiana, Sampdoria's victory kept them in the hunt for a place in next season's Champions league.

Two goals from Vincenzo Montella, taking his tally to 16 in 17 matches, and another from Marco Carparelli assured Sampdoria of their first league win since defeating Milan at the San Siro on February 2.
Sampdoria fans staged a 30 second silence to protest the four-game suspension of Yugoslav sweeper Sinisa Mihajlovic, sent off last week for aiming the ball at a referee.
The victory sent the Genoa club over Inter into third-spot, four points adrift of Parma and the runners-up position which guarantees qualification for the Champions' League.

Juventus remain a cut above the rest - five points clear of Parma - shrugging off the absence of Alen Boksic and Alessandro Del Piero to thrash Roma with two goals from fill-in centre-forward Christian Vieri.
